findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspector observed an accumulation of grease on the hood baffles in the back section of the kitchen. This build up could serve as an ignition source for a kitchen fire. Physical facilities must be cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of grease or other debris. Clean by next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.comment: No Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM/ CFM) was present during today's inspection. A CFM is required at all establishments serving unpackaged food to oversee food handling, proper hot and cold holding temperatures for temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods, as well as proper sanitation procedures and concentrations. Ensure a CFM is acquired and present for future inspections.
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager. (A) The PERSON IN 
CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
A mop was observed stored in the mop bucket.  Discussed with PIC.  Ensure mops are stored in a way to allow them to properly air dry.

6-501.16: After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to airdry without soiling walls, EQUIPMENT, or supplies.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
Back exterior door has a small gap allowing daylight through.  Discussed with PIC.  Ensure outer openings are sealed to protect against pest and rodent entry.

6-202.15: (A) Outer openings of FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against entry of insects and rodents. (B) Does not apply to FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS which opens into larger structure. (C) Exterior doors need not be self-closing if designed for limited-use. (D) If opening present, opening shall be protected against rodent and insects. (E) Paragraph (D) not applicable when pests are absent.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
No temperature measuring device was available.  Discussed with PIC, who ordered a temperature measuring disk at time of inspection.  Ensure disk is on-site and available to check temperature of heat sanitation to properly sanitize dishes.

4-204.115: A WAREWASHING machine shall be equipped with a TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE that indicates the temperature of the water: (A) In each wash and rinse tank; (B) As the water enters the hot water SANITIZING final rinse manifold or in the chemical SANITIZING solution tank.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Ice machine baffles were observed to contain mold/mildew.  Discussed with PIC.  Ensure ice baffles are cleaned regularly to prevent ice contamination.

4-602.11: (D) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned less than every 4 hours if in storage of food within proper temperatures, food is prepared in refrigerated room, if practice has regulatory approval, or UTENSILS stored in 135F water. (E) Surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting food shall be cleaned any time contamination occurs, at least 24 hours for certain UTENSILS (i.e. iced tea dispensers), before restocking self-service EQUIPMENT, in EQUIPMENT such as ice bins in frequency to prevent mold. At a frequency to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Hot and cold water available; adequate pressure
findings.comment:
5-103.12: The service sink in the fry room is not currently in-use and water has been terminated while refresh completes. See that water is restored prior to use in March. WM will spot check. Changing to Core violation as kitchen space isn't in-use until Lenten fish fries begin and WM will check on correction before that start. 

Water under pressure shall be provided to all fixtures, EQUIPMENT, and nonFOOD EQUIPMENT that are required to use water except that water (A) and (B) to a TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT or in response to a temporary interruption of a water supply need not be under pressure.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Upon start of inspection, it was discovered that a shelf liner was placed along counter to left of sink, to keep dishes from sliding off counter while they dry.  Shelf liner was peeled back to discover water and mold had accumulated under liner.  CORRECTED - church administrative assistant removed liner and alternatives for air drying (including clean and sanitized bar mesh, or cafeteria trays) were discussed.  This counter top surface should be smooth and easily cleanable.

750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
The following non-food contact surfaces are soiled:
(a) knife sharpener in main kitchen cabinet (food splash), 
(b) surfaces around the blade of the table-mounted can opener, 
(c) top of Vulcan Oven (KoC Rm) (REPEAT), 
(d) floor of cabinet below hand sink (KoC Rm) (kitty-litter-type substance?) (REPEAT), 
(e) shelves of metal spice cabinet (KoC Rm) (REPEAT x2), 
(f) shelves of lower cabinet holding baking pans and powdered cleansers.
Clean and maintain these surfaces throughout Lenten fish fries, and throughout the year.  All surfaces around fryer units, including surfaces inside lower panels, are incredibly clean.  Keep up these good fryer-cleaning practices.

750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
The following floors are soiled:
(a) under the ovens/stoves in main kitchen, 
(b) under shelves in dry storage room (REPEAT x2), 
(c) under full length of fryers in KoC Room (REPEAT x2).
Clean and maintain these floors.  Even though this is the busy Lenten fish fry season, try to maintain the floors clean of oil and debris in the same manner the lower fryer surfaces are maintained.  Given recent history with pests, kitchen and KoC room floors should be maintained clean of food debris and oil to eliminate food source for potential pests.

750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment: The following clean equipment was uncovered/unprotected and/or soiled:  (A) trays in cabinet to lower-left of pass-thru window, (B) utensils in cup (should be stored w/ food-contact surfaces down), (C) island utensil drawers (stored with food-contact surfaces and handles intermixed).  Re-position and/or protect this clean equipment.                          750-860 Cleaned & sanitized utensils/equipment shall be stored at least 6" above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means.     750-850 Cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils shall be handled in a way that protects them from contamination.  Spoons, knives and forks shall be touched only by their handles.  Cups glasses, bowls, plates and similar items shall be handled without contact with inside surfaces.

Also, make sure to protect coffee stir sticks if they are stored in coffee mugs.

750-880 Single-service articles shall be handled and dispensed in a manner which prevents contamination of surfaces which may come in contact with food or with the mouth of the user.
